# uptimeify_customer_ip (Resource)

An IP address of a customer, checked against DNS blocklists (DNSBL). Creating one that already exists with the same values fails; import it instead. Import with the numeric id or the public id.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "uptimeify_customer_ip" "mail" {
  customer_id = tonumber(uptimeify_customer.shop.id)
  ip_address  = "203.0.113.25"
  label       = "Mail server"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `customer_id` (Number)
- `ip_address` (String) IPv4 or IPv6 address, lower case.

### Optional

- `ip_family` (String) `v4` or `v6`; derived from the address when unset.
- `label` (String)
- `management_type` (String) `managed` or `self_service`. Only organization writers choose it; customer-scoped tokens always create `self_service` entries, everyone else gets `managed` when unset.
- `status` (String) `active` (checked, counts against the IP quota) or `disabled`.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String)
- `id` (String) Numeric id.
- `public_id` (String)
- `updated_at` (String)

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Numeric id or public id
terraform import uptimeify_customer_ip.mail 7
```
